Model summary

Projection 6.48 Ks vs line 7.5 · edge 20.3pp to the under (model 67% / market 47%) · conviction tier · 6 books, best −103 (BetOnline). Stake at the time: $200; under the current deployment guard this play would be PAPER.

Qualitative confirmation

  • Workload management is the whole story. Detroit capped Skubal at 80–96 pitches in each of his last five starts (IP: 4.2, 5.2, 6.0, 5.0) — he had not completed the 6th inning in a month. At ~1.5 K/IP, a 5–6 inning outing supports ~7 Ks only in a best-case game; 8+ requires depth Detroit was not allowing.
  • Last start before the All-Star break — the classic short-leash spot; no incentive to extend an ace about to get four days of rest.
  • Opponent contact profile neutral: Phillies lineup K-rate vs LHP 22.3% prior / 22.4% last-14 — dead league average. Nothing in the matchup argues for an outlier K night.
  • Umpire mildly under-friendly: Edwin Moscoso's prior called-strike rate runs 0.6pp below league expectation.

Contradictory evidence

  • Stuff fully intact: velocity flat (92.6 → 92.9 last 3 starts), elite 18.7% SwStr / 30.5% CSW; two 9-K games in his previous four starts — the over's tail was live if he worked into the 7th.
  • Comerica plays K-friendly (park SO factor 1.10; venue prior 4.77 Ks/start); warm calm night, no weather suppression.

Verdict

Moderate qualitative confirmation — the edge priced the pitcher's leash, not his stuff. Settled: 5 Ks in 5+ IP, pulled to lead off the 6th; the under won on exactly the workload mechanism.

Model summary

Projection 4.3 Ks vs line 2.5 · edge +19.3pp over · CONV · −145 (6 books). PAPER under the deployment guard.

Qualitative confirmation

  • The line (2.5) sits far below his per-start K range — he posted 2+ Ks in every recent start (2,4,4,4).

Contradictory evidence

  • 18 days since his last start — a layoff that long usually means injury/skipped turns and a hard pitch limit on return; a 60–75 pitch outing can strand him at 2–3 Ks.
  • Weak bat-missing profile (8.2% SwStr) and St. Louis is a below-average K offense (19.6% season, 21.5% L15).
  • Heavy juice (−145) at only ~4 expected innings of runway.

Verdict

Mixed signals

Projection 4.9 Ks vs line 5.5 · edge 18.3pp under · CONV · +110 (7 books). PAPER under the deployment guard.

Qualitative confirmation

  • Quick-hook profile: 5 of his last 10 starts went under 5 IP, average only 86 pitches — the 6+ K over needs length he rarely gets.
  • Exceeded 5 Ks just once in his last four pre-game starts (4,5,4,7).
  • Velocity readings drifting down ~1mph across recent starts — no sign of a stuff spike.

Contradictory evidence

  • Cincinnati strikes out a LOT — 26.4% of PAs over the last 15 games (league 22.5%) — the single biggest risk to any under against them.

Verdict

Moderate qualitative confirmation

Qualitative confirmation

No strong qualitative confirmation found beyond the model edge.

Contradictory evidence

  • The workload argument does not apply to Wheeler: zero short starts in his last 10, 96–104 pitches every time out, 6–7 IP routinely — Philadelphia lets him finish what he starts.
  • Elite whiff form (18.1% SwStr, 31.2% CSW) and he cleared this line twice in his last four (9, 14 Ks).
  • Detroit's K rate is league-average — no contact-heavy shield.

Verdict

Neutral (model-only edge)

Model summary

Projection 4.2 Ks vs line 3.5 · edge +11.2pp over · base · +112 (7 books). PAPER under the deployment guard.

Qualitative confirmation

  • Classic injury-return ramp: pitch counts climbing every start (20 → 60 → 74 → 79 → 82) — the next step is 85–90 pitches, meaningfully more K runway than the line implies.
  • Velocity recovering alongside it, with a healthy 14.9% SwStr.
  • Texas Ks at a slightly above-average clip (23.1% L15).

Contradictory evidence

  • He hasn't actually exceeded 4 Ks in any start since returning — the over needs the ramp to continue, not just hold.

Moderate qualitative confirmation

Qualitative confirmation

  • Cleared this line in four straight pre-game starts (5,6,6,8).
  • Deep leash: 95 pitches/start average with only 1 short start in 10 — plenty of runway.
  • Cubs' K rate has run above average recently (24.4% L15), and the umpire leans marginally K-friendly.

Moderate qualitative confirmation
